ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #2
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. going
   B. goes
   C. goed
   D. went

2. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.

3. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only an action
   B. Only a joining word
   C. Only a describing word
   D. A person, place, thing, or idea

4. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. No full stops
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. Many unrelated topics with no link
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

5. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

6. When practising Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

7. When practising Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

8. When practising Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.

9. When practising Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.

10. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. run
   B. quickly
   C. happiness
   D. blue

11. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. where is the library
   B. Where is the library?
   C. Where is the Library
   D. Where is the library

12. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Spelling and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Pronunciation and Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — went

2. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.

3. D — A person, place, thing, or idea

4. D — One main idea with supporting sentences

5. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

6. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

7. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

8. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.

9. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.

10. A — run

11. B — Where is the library?

12. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Spelling; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Pronunciation and Vocabulary; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
